description: Permits shared e-scooters on public right-of-way.
City will select up to two e-scooter vendors.
Bylaw 7200 will be amended for e-scooter operation.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor Ford questioned low bylaw enforcement (4 tickets in two years).
Local businesses benefited from $5.6 million in e-scooter rider spending.
City Solicitor noted the limited permit process was unusual for the city.
Administration did not know why few companies applied for e-scooter permits.
Councillor Pearce flagged a $5,000 vehicle damage claim denied by Neuron Mobility.
Disabled residents reported scooters blocking access on sidewalks and crosswalks.
Neuron stated about half of e-scooter trips replace car journeys.
Neuron Mobility offered to engage with the Accessibility Advisory Committee.

segments.title: Economic impact of e-scooter program
description: High ridership led to significant economic impact.
Over 10% of trips wouldn't have occurred otherwise.
Riders spend approximately $58 at local businesses per trip.
Total economic impact was $5.6 million last year.

chips.text: $5.6 million economic impact over the last year
local businesses in Saskatoon

Riders must return scooters to designated "P" spots.
Preferred parking areas outside restricted zones offer incentives.

chips.text: geo-fencing used for no parking and slow ride zones

segments.title: End-of-trip parking and safety checks
description: Riders guided to green parking areas to end trips.
Sequence includes helmet return, area scan, and photo.
Technology recognizes street features and location.
Scooters cannot end trip if not parked upright.

chips.text: scooter sensors detect if not parked upright

chips.text: Neuron provides a helmet on every single device
e-scooter riders in Saskatoon
